dependency_self_check.monotonicity_usage: Used monotonicity of floor and positivity of k to compare each summand.
dependency_self_check.scope: Only the stated lemma was used.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix n>1 and an integer m with 0<=m<=n-1. Let x,y be real numbers such that m/n<=x<=y<(m+1)/n. Then m<=nx<=ny<m+1, so floor(nx)=floor(ny)=m. Also, for each k=1,2,...,n, since x<=y and k>0 we have kx<=ky, hence floor(kx)<=floor(ky). Therefore
F_n(x)-F_n(y) = (floor(nx)-floor(ny)) - sum_{k=1}^n (floor(kx)-floor(ky))/k
= sum_{k=1}^n (floor(ky)-floor(kx))/k >= 0,
because each summand is nonnegative and each k is positive. Thus F_n(x)>=F_n(y), so F_n is nonincreasing on [m/n,(m+1)/n).
result_payload.proof_summary: On the interval [m/n,(m+1)/n), the term floor(nx) is constant, while each floor(kx) is nondecreasing in x; hence the whole expression cannot increase.

used_external_facts: If a<=b and c>0, then ac<=bc.
The floor function is nondecreasing: u<=v implies floor(u)<=floor(v).
If an integer q satisfies m<=q<m+1, then q=m.
